match_note: arXiv v1 (June 2026) matches the final revised manuscript, not the one first reviewed. v1 already contains text added during review: the title 'Multiple Hole Fermi Pockets' (the rebuttal says it replaced 'hole Fermi pockets only'); 'strong antiferromagnetic order and correlations' in the abstract; 'The α Fermi surface is more consistent with a hole pocket'; the sentences on the limited momentum range and on AFM correlations; the coherence-temperature discussion of the lower Tc; the IP1 gap discussion; the citation of Narita et al. for Tc; the NMR long-range-AFM paragraph; and the Fig. 6a of [49] OP argument. Fig. 1j has the edge artifacts cropped. One remnant of the original framing survives in the Discussion: 'our present observation of Fermi pockets only indicates...'. Five rounds of referee reports: V0 (R1, R2, R3), V1 (R1, R2, R3; R3's report is in the attachment), V2 (R1, R3), V3 (R1), V4 (R1).

concerns.quote: the α Fermi surface cannot be unambiguously confirmed to be hole-pocket-like, but could also be part of a large Fermi surface, due to the insufficient k range accessible in the laser ARPES experiment.
concerns.summary: The limited momentum coverage means the α (and per R2 also β) Fermi surface may be part of a large Fermi surface rather than a closed hole pocket.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Do the authors consider that the blue contour on the folded part [beyond the (π, 0)-(0,π) line] of the “hole pocket” is intrinsic signals or experimental artefact?
concerns.summary: Intensity beyond the (π,0)-(0,π) line and near Γ in Fig. 1j (asymmetric and sharper than the main Fermi surface) may be detector-edge artifacts rather than evidence of pocket closure.

concerns.quote: The superconducting gap opening in the CuO2 planes that are not adjacent to the OP, i.e., in IP1, is the first observation in multi-layer cuprates.
concerns.summary: The authors should highlight and discuss the origin and implications of the large gap in IP1, a plane not adjacent to OP.

concerns.quote: since the Tc of Bi2267 is lower than Bi2223 (and possibly Bi2245 and Bi2256), it would be worthwhile to discuss how the lower Tc of Bi2267 is related to the pairing gaps
concerns.summary: The large pairing gaps need to be reconciled with Bi2267's lower Tc compared with Bi2223.

concerns.quote: the spectra from Region 2 even show some traces of replica band feature marked as SSα and SSβ. How can the authors distinguish the trace of original Fermi surface from the replica?
concerns.summary: Superstructure replica bands might be confused with the main Fermi surface pockets.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the dashed lines in Fig. 1k, which comprises closed pocket, might mislead the readers.
concerns.summary: Drawing closed pockets in Fig. 1k overstates what the data show.

concerns.quote: It is unclearly described what the authors would like to highlight with this comment.
concerns.summary: The point of the sentence on distinct doping dependence of nodal kF for pockets versus large Fermi surfaces (Fig. 1l) is unclear.

concerns.quote: Determination of the peak position is not explicit. It is in some sense hand-waving... no opening of superconducting gap in the δ band is not clearly proven.
concerns.summary: EDC peak assignments in Fig. 3 ignore visible shoulders and humps, so the gap values and the claimed gapless δ pocket are not rigorously established.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: it is unclear whether pseudogap is particle-hole symmetric or not... I recommend that authors divide the spectra by the resolution convoluted Fermi function
concerns.summary: Symmetrization assumes particle-hole symmetry, so the gap and pseudogap analysis in Figs. 3 and 4 should be cross-checked by Fermi-function division.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the authors plot the temperature dependent EDC of all the bands except that of δ band.
concerns.summary: Temperature-dependent EDCs for the δ band should be shown.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: there is no description how authors are sure that the antiferromagnetism does not enter the spin fluctuation region.
concerns.summary: The claim of long-range AFM order (not short-range or fluctuating) in IP1/IP0 is unsupported; the authors should check for coexisting folded and unfolded band branches.

concerns.quote: the location of alphabets on the figure panel is not consistent.
concerns.summary: Panel labels in Figs. 1 and 3 are misaligned.

concerns.quote: the color code indicating each temperature gives some confusion in tracking the temperature dependent feature.
concerns.summary: The temperature color coding in Figs. 4c-h should be more intuitive.

concerns.quote: this is not a sufficient determination of Tc in the cuprates due to fluctuating superconductivity.
concerns.summary: Tc ~75 K is inferred from gap closure and spectral weight, not a thermodynamic signature, and the in-gap intensity singularity of ref. 57 is not shown.

concerns.quote: It is possible that the 7-layer region is only 1 or 2 unit cells thick and can be proximitized by the trilayer BSCCO below.
concerns.summary: The gaps in the thin 7-layer intergrowth might be proximity-induced by the surrounding 109 K Bi2223.

concerns.quote: The size of the reconstructed pocket and the nodal kF are influenced by both the doping level p, as well as the strength of the reconstructing order
concerns.summary: Pocket area is not a valid doping label for reconstructed pockets, so the doping comparison with 2- and 3-layer BSCCO in Fig. 5l is unjustified.

concerns.quote: the antinodal region is not actually directly measured. I think this may be a bit too ambitious of a claim.
concerns.summary: The claim that only nodal pocket states exist is unsupported; antinodal states may remain, especially in the disordered OP, for example via nanoscale phase separation.

concerns.quote: why the gaps are much larger than the 5- and 6-layer compounds in references [36, 37], even at the same nominal “doping” obtained by the pocket size.
concerns.summary: The authors should explain why the gaps far exceed those of 5- and 6-layer cuprates at the same nominal doping.

later_concerns.quote: it is not clear whether all the artefact has been removed or some still remains near the removed part.
later_concerns.summary: (Round 2) Cropping Fig. 1j may not have removed all detector-edge artifacts.

later_concerns.quote: the α Fermi surface in Fig. 1c, d, f, and g may be better fitted with the large Fermi surface model rather than the hole pocket model.
later_concerns.summary: (Round 2) The hole-pocket fit misfits the data; large-FS fits should be tried and the 'hole pocket only' claim removed if they work better.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: First of all, the kinetic term should have a plus sign instead of a minus sign.
later_concerns.summary: (Round 2) Sign error in the mean-field Hamiltonian in the Supplement.

later_concerns.quote: This is clearly still a model involving Fermi surface reconstruction... the size of the pockets in this model can be independently controlled by μ and ΔMF
later_concerns.summary: (Round 2) The authors' t-U mean-field model is itself AF-like reconstruction, so pocket size still does not equal doping.

later_concerns.quote: I believe the authors misused these references to reach an incorrect conclusion. Actually, I think these references lend support to the FS reconstruction scenario.
later_concerns.summary: (Round 2) Refs. 61-65 do not support the claim that the t-U picture excludes Fermi surface reconstruction.

later_concerns.quote: either the authors’ model is wrong, or the work by Kunisada et al cannot be used in this argument.
later_concerns.summary: (Round 2) The t-U simulation predicts (π,0) states within 0.5 eV, inconsistent with Kunisada et al.'s 70 eV data cited as evidence of no antinodal states.

later_concerns.quote: It is possible that 7 eV is not sensitive to the large FS states in this system. Without a detailed synchrotron measurement involving different photon energies
later_concerns.summary: (Round 2) Small pockets and a large Fermi surface could coexist in the OP; photon-energy-dependent synchrotron data covering the antinodal region are needed.

later_concerns.quote: The constant energy contour well above EF (EF + 30 meV, EF + 50 meV) is influenced by dynamical (correlation) effects and, therefore, does not guarantee the shape of the Fermi surface at EF.
later_concerns.summary: (Round 3) Contours above EF cannot establish the Fermi surface topology at EF.

later_concerns.quote: If a smaller t' is employed in the tight-binding model used for the extrapolation of the Fermi surface to the antinodal region, the estimated doping level would become significantly higher.
later_concerns.summary: (Round 3) The implausibly low 0.025 doping from the large-FS fit is model-dependent and does not rule out a large Fermi surface.

later_concerns.quote: some likely scenario has to be proposed as to how such an unprecedentedly large pocket as ~0.12-0.14 hole content has become possible.
later_concerns.summary: (Round 3) No mechanism is given for a hole pocket at such high doping.

later_concerns.quote: The hole-pocket-like electronic structure above ~EF + 30 meV and a large Fermi surface at EF can co-exist under the (energy- and momentum-dependent) self-energy
later_concerns.summary: (Round 4) Dynamical AFM correlations rather than static order could produce the pocket-like dispersion while a large Fermi surface exists at EF.

later_concerns.quote: This uncertainty and the resulting ambiguity in the interpretation of the OP Fermi surface should not be ignored and should be honestly discussed in the paper.
later_concerns.summary: (Round 4) OP doping could be up to ~0.1 under the large-FS picture, and this ambiguity must be discussed.

later_concerns.quote: the same NMR study has indeed shown that the OP is paramagnetic up to n=8 (optimally-doped Hg1278), see Fig. 19 of [49]
later_concerns.summary: (Round 4) The cited NMR work contradicts static AFM order in the OP.

later_concerns.quote: One of the red circle on the edge of the field of view is not located at an intensity maximum
later_concerns.summary: (Round 5) A mis-placed extracted point biases the fit; the SM claim should be restricted to the EF+30 meV contour, not the Fermi surface.

later_concerns.quote: needs to explicitly mention the possibility of strong AFM correlations in addition to AFM order as the origin of hole pocket-like behavior.
later_concerns.summary: (Round 5) The text must explicitly state dynamical AFM correlations as an alternative interpretation.

later_concerns.quote: Abstract: “strong antiferromagnetic order” should be “strong antiferromagnetic order and correlations”.
Make the dashed curve of the α Fermi pocket a thinner curve.
later_concerns.summary: (Round 5) De-emphasize the α pocket outline in Figs. 1, 2 and 4.

later_concerns.quote: “Four (Fermi) pockets” in many places should be replaced by “(Fermi) pockets” since “four” means that the α Fermi surface has already been established to be a Fermi pocket.
later_concerns.summary: (Round 5) Wording implies the α pocket is established; it should be softened throughout.
